clue.text: In line with law introduced by one legislator? Not in so many words

indicators.note: something introduced by another comes after it, so the legislator part goes in front

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
Member of Parliament
lawful, permitted by law

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is lawful once a single legislator brings it in.
explanation.walkthrough: The lawful phrase comes first in the clue but last in the answer, because it is introduced by, so preceded by, the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is implied or understood rather than stated outright, so it is never put into so many words.

clue.text: A nightly appearance, but not by star

definitions.text: A nightly appearance, but not by star

parts.words: A nightly appearance, but not by star
parts.note: surface reading: a celebrity's evening show that some performer other than the headliner gives
setter's reading: a heavenly body coming up over the horizon each night that is not a star but a satellite

explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a headline performer making a nightly stage appearance; the real body appearing is in the sky, and it is not a star at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon rising above the horizon is a regular night-time appearance in the sky, and the moon is a satellite rather than a star.

clue.text: Thames landmark, from vantage point on vessel author's on

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that is on another sits above it, so the writer's name comes first

parts.note: Jack London, American author of The Call of the Wild
the raised platform from which a ship is commanded

explanation.surface: A view of a Thames landmark from the deck of a ship carrying a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack London was an American novelist; the bridge of a ship is its command platform. The famous bridge crosses the Thames in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: The bridge of that name is a well-known crossing of the River Thames in the City of London.

clue.text: Caught bird — chicken?

parts.note: the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
a large black bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A bird has been caught, and someone wonders whether it is a chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' looks like the bird in question, but here it is the slang for a coward; the question mark flags that switch.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken as an adjective is slang for cowardly, and craven means lacking courage.

clue.text: Ruler finally executed in drastic uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising letters are read from the bottom up
the letters sit inside a single word of the clue

parts.note: the middle letters of this word

explanation.surface: A monarch put to death at last during a violent revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is extended: Nicholas II, the last of Russia's emperors, was finally shot by revolutionaries in 1918.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Russian emperor, the last of whom was executed after the Russian Revolution.

clue.text: At sea, a pilot? No, not required

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a pilot is needed on a ship and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark breaks the surface but the fodder runs straight across it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something optional is left to choice, so it is not compulsory or required.

clue.text: Notice little good in what's bad

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing
G is the short form of good

explanation.surface: Observe that there is scant good in something wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' is a noun here, as in a notice pinned to a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A posted notice and a sign are both boards or placards giving information.

clue.text: Duke feeling reduction in status

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
a feeling such as joy or anger

explanation.surface: A nobleman's feelings about being lowered in rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A demotion is a move down to a lower rank or position, the opposite of promotion.

clue.text: Perhaps I damaged precious stone

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone admits they may have damaged a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapphire is a precious gem, usually blue, a variety of the mineral corundum.

clue.text: Audibly disapprove of new gift

parts.note: to jeer out loud
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone loudly objects to a present they have just been given.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a blessing or benefit, something given that is welcome.

clue.text: Piece of music Verdi arranged, with tempo not changed

indicators.note: arranging means putting in a new order, as a composer arranges a score

parts.note: the Italian opera composer's name, taken as written

indicators.note: a second signal: these letters too are altered in their order

parts.note: tempo and time both mean the pace or rhythm of music
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musical work by Verdi has been arranged, but the speed is left alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tempo not changed' seems to mean the tempo stays the same; in fact tempo is TIME, and it is the word not that gets changed.
explanation.definitionFit: A divertimento is a light instrumental composition of several movements, popular in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Performer who's bound to start act, but not to finish it

definitions.text: Performer who's bound to start act, but not to finish it

parts.note: surface reading: a performer who is certain to open the show
setter's reading: the performer is tied up in chains at the start, and must be free by the end

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'sure to'; really it means literally tied up, like Houdini at the start of his escape act.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapologist is an entertainer who frees themselves from ropes, chains or locked boxes in front of an audience.

clue.text: Part of test on wife showing pounds gained, say

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, so the test part comes second

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
a Test match in cricket is divided into innings, each side's turn to bat

explanation.surface: A cricket fan's wife watches part of a Test and gains weight.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match, played over several innings. 'Pounds gained' suggests weight; it is money won.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnings are money won by gambling or competition, so pounds gained are an example, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Capital, we hear, doubled for solitary individual

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, not written
doubled says the one sound stands in for two different words at once

parts.note: said out loud, the city's name matches both solitary (sole) and individual (soul), so it is doubled

explanation.surface: A capital city stood in for, as we are told, a lone person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubled' is the clever part: the sound fits two words at once, one for each of the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Seoul is the capital city of South Korea.

clue.text: Central pieces revised in clue

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Key parts of a crossword clue have been rewritten.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclei, the plural of nucleus, are the central cores of atoms, cells or anything built around a centre.

clue.text: Queen bee improperly ordered drink

indicators.note: things improperly ordered are out of sequence, so the letters need rearranging

parts.note: R for Regina, Latin for queen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A queen bee orders a drink she should not have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen bee' reads as one insect, but the queen is split off as R.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer is an alcoholic drink brewed from malted grain and hops.

clue.text: Old composer heard, then modern one, in arrangement of bars for singer

indicators.note: heard means the name is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: William Byrd, Tudor composer, whose name sounds like a feathered creature
John Cage, twentieth-century American composer

explanation.surface: Two composers, an old and a modern one, combine on a musical arrangement of bars for a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' and 'singer' sound musical but mean metal rods and a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A birdcage is a set of bars put together to hold a songbird such as a canary.

clue.text: Indication of canine discontent — get bigger pound

parts.note: to increase in size
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A dog shows unhappiness at a dogs' pound growing larger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' suggests a dog pound; here it is the money.
explanation.definitionFit: A growl is the low rumbling noise a dog makes when angry or unhappy.

clue.text: Shrub with fragrant flowers, possibly changing to red again

indicators.note: something possibly changing may take another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A flowering shrub whose blooms might turn red once more.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardenia is an evergreen shrub prized for its heavily scented white flowers.

clue.text: Man on board making deposit for a loan

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the lowest-ranking chess piece
second meaning: an item left as security when borrowing money

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a sailor; in chess the pieces are called men.
explanation.definitionFit: The chess piece and the pledge left with a pawnbroker share a name.

clue.text: Its majority shareholder can ask for anything, supposedly

definitions.text: Its majority shareholder can ask for anything, supposedly

parts.note: surface reading: the person owning most shares in a company
setter's reading: two people pull a forked bone from a chicken, and whoever gets the larger piece makes a wish

explanation.walkthrough: The business language misleads: the 'majority share' is the bigger piece of the bone, and the superstition is that its holder's wish comes true.
explanation.definitionFit: The wishbone is the forked bone of a bird, pulled apart by two people for luck after a meal.

clue.text: Further to left? In either direction, it's the same

parts.words: In either direction, it's the same
parts.note: the second half describes the word's form: it reads the same forwards and backwards

explanation.surface: Is this further to the left? Either way you look at it, nothing changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a direction; it is politics, where red stands for socialism.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is the colour of socialism, so someone more left-wing is said to be redder.

clue.text: Make catalogue that's shorter and lacking oomph

parts.note: to list is to make an itemised catalogue
less, smaller in amount

explanation.surface: Someone compiles a shortened catalogue that is dull and flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless means having no energy or enthusiasm, without vigour or oomph.

clue.text: Bad mark from oddly sitting half of exam when upset

indicators.note: oddly means taking the letters in odd-numbered positions

parts.note: letters one, three, five and seven

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read from the bottom
half of a word keeps just two of its four letters

parts.note: the second half of the word

explanation.surface: A poor grade from sitting half an exam while distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace attached to someone, a figurative blot or brand.

clue.text: Encouraging holding copies back — that's mean

indicators.note: one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: giving cheers of support

indicators.note: going back means reading the word from right to left

parts.note: to ape is to copy or imitate

explanation.surface: Supporting those who keep copies held back, which is a stingy thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheeseparing describes extreme stinginess, as if paring the rind off cheese to save every scrap.

clue.text: Be paid twice in year, near November

indicators.note: the same short word sits inside two words of the clue, once in each

parts.note: the last three letters of the first word, and also the last three of the second
November is N in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Getting paid twice a year, close to November.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to receive money in return for work, to be paid.

clue.text: Penniless receivers of money handed over as charity

indicators.note: without a penny means the abbreviation for penny is dropped

parts.note: palms are the hands' insides, which receive money, as in greasing someone's palm

explanation.surface: Destitute people receiving cash given to them in charity.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the standard abbreviation for penny, so a penniless word loses its P.
explanation.definitionFit: Alms are money or food given to the poor as charitable donations.

clue.text: Something on computer screen the writer scans

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themself as I
to con is to study or pore over; with I it becomes 'I con', the same as the writer scans

explanation.surface: A writer looks over something displayed on a computer screen.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a small picture on a computer desktop that opens a program or file when clicked.

clue.text: Asian queen cutting plant or flower

indicators.note: a piece cutting into another slices into its middle

parts.note: geum is a flowering plant of the rose family
a rani is an Indian queen or a rajah's wife

explanation.surface: An Asian queen cuts a plant or a flower in her garden.
explanation.walkthrough: GEUM is a garden plant often seen in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The geranium is a popular garden and pot plant grown for its bright flowers.

clue.text: Taken by surprise, began pulling in line

indicators.note: pulling something in draws it inside

parts.note: started means began
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone surprised when they started dragging in a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To be startled is to be given a sudden shock or fright by something unexpected.
